patch.value: credential_key_assignment still treats a value that starts with a reference as a placeholder, so api_key=${EMPTY}"<credential>" and literal defaults pass, and the key-named rules disagree on a bare $VAR

Found 2026-11-17 while fixing pm-ycgb5g. The credential_key_assignment value grammar (CREDENTIAL_VALUE in src/core/shared/secret-rules.ts) still excludes every value whose first characters are a reference or placeholder ($, <, ${, $(), so a literal concatenated with a reference is never judged: api_key=${EMPTY}"<credential>", api_key=$VAR"<credential>", "client_secret": "${EMPTY}<credential>", token: <x><credential> and the literal default api_key=${KEY:-<credential>} all pass the SDK guard (measured with scanMutationSecrets on the 2026-11-16 build; api_key=<credential>${VAR} is already detected). pm-ycgb5g fixed the same hole for password_assignment with a whole-value rule: the value is captured whole and minimumLiteralLength judges literalAfterReferences, the literal left once references expand to nothing. The two key-named rules now also disagree on a bare $VAR reference: password=$DB_PASSWORD is still reported by password_assignment, while api_key=$API_KEY is allowed by credential_key_assignment. Fix direction: give credential_key_assignment the same whole-value reference judgment (entropy measured on the literal after references expand), and decide one bare-$VAR policy for both rules with a must-allow entry for shell variables. credential_key_assignment is mutation-only, so the false-positive check is the pm-1l85at corpus rather than the repository scan. Duplicate check: searched credential_key_assignment reference placeholder concatenated literal; pm-ycgb5g (password rule only) and pm-jcz7qz (adversarial corpus) are related, and neither owns the credential-key reference grammar.

credential_key_assignment judges a value by the literal left once run-time references expand to nothing, so a literal before or after a reference and a literal default are refused in text, quoted-key and object-payload spellings; A bare ${API_KEY}, $(op read key), <placeholder> and an empty default stay allowed, and one documented bare-$VAR policy applies to both password_assignment and credential_key_assignment; The pm-1l85at false-positive corpus and the pm-gh1704 must-allow corpus stay clean and the linear-time controls still pass
A credential concatenated with a reference is refused by every key-named rule
credential_key_assignment skips any value that starts with a reference or placeholder
